subject: Tailored rate carveout for LunarMed pilot — VP/CFO signoff requested
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tailored rate carveout for LunarMed pilot — VP/CFO signoff requested

Team — looping you in on a commercial ask that we need quick internal alignment on. LunarMed (Sam Jenkins / Priya Rao) is ready to commit to a 24-month Dedicated + Private deployment agreement but needs a one-time tailored rate to cover an aggressive pilot/onboarding window. Key facts:  

- Ask: 55% blended discount on Dedicated unit rates for months 0–6, stepping to 30% months 7–12, then 15% thereafter; includes a $150k onboarding credit to cover integration and SOC attestation prep.
- Value: Targeted ACV $2.1M; first-year recognized revenue ~ $860k (after discounts & credits).
- Strategic: Healthcare logo, priority region (US-East), strong reference potential for our Private offering in regulated verticals.
- Risk: Heavy initial discount skews first-year margin; requires contractual guardrails (commit thresholds + clawback).

Attached: pricing worksheet (LunarMed_Pricing_Worksheet_v3.xlsx) with modeled outcomes and a proposed SOW draft.

I need VP/CFO-level signoff on a carveout to offer this structure (it sits outside our standard rate guardrails). Proposed guardrails we think are necessary for signoff:
- 70%-of-committed-usage threshold over the first 6 months, otherwise a pro-rata recoup on discounts;
- Minimum 12-month firm commit to trigger the onboarding credit;
- Legal to add an auto-fallback to hosted model at published rates if private deployment delays exceed 90 days.

Can you review quickly? Ben — from a sales perspective, this keeps the deal live this quarter. Marissa — need finance perspective on margin and language you want in the memo. Laura — please flag any legal/contract points we should require prior to signoff.

I’ll be on the call with LunarMed Monday AM; want to give the customer a definitive answer by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: LunarMed_Pricing_Worksheet_v3.xlsx)

(quoted: "On Fri, 23 Apr 2027 at 09:12, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:")

Subject: Re: Tailored rate carveout for LunarMed pilot — VP/CFO signoff requested

Soojin — thanks for the clear summary and the worksheet. Quick notes:  

- Commercial rationale checks out: they’re leaning into us because of our Private compliance packaging plus roadmap alignment. Won’t be easy to replace if we lose the timing.
- From a sales ops POV I’d prefer to keep the % discount lower if we can get the onboarding credit to cover implementation pain points (i.e., shift dollars from % discount into a one-time credit).

Marissa / Markus — do we have a rough IRR or payback threshold we want to hit for a deal of this profile? I modeled simple scenarios in the attached worksheet but want finance’s view before offering anything concrete.

Also flag: customer is asking for a three-month implementation SLA and immediate access to audit logs; legal may want to tighten data-handling language.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales
(quoted: "On Fri, 23 Apr 2027 at 09:12, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:")

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tailored rate carveout for LunarMed pilot — VP/CFO signoff requested

Thanks for the heads up and the worksheet — reviewed. Summary from finance:  

- Baseline: at 55% initial discount + $150k credit our blended gross margin for year 1 drops to ~17% (model assumptions attached). That is below our typical strategic-account threshold (we normally target >=30% blended gross margin for dedicated contracts).
- Upside if usage ramps: if LunarMed achieves >=85% of committed units by month 6, blended margin improves to ~28% by year-end.

Recommended alternate structure to reduce downside risk:  
1) Move to 40% discount months 0–6 (instead of 55%) + a $150k onboarding credit tied to milestone acceptance (deliverables: audit readiness checklist, SSO integration complete).
2) Include a 6-month usage ramp schedule in the SOW; if they miss the 70% usage threshold at month 6 we recoup onboarding credit pro rata and step discounts back to published tiers.
3) Require finance review of monthly usage reports for first 12 months and a quarterly executive review clause.

I attached a short finance memo summarizing margin impact and the wording we prefer for clawbacks. If leadership wants to go deeper on competitive/strategic rationale we can append an incremental ROI scenario — but that will take 24–48 hours.

Attached: finance_memo_lunarmed_20270425.pdf

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Finance
(quoted: "On Fri, 23 Apr 2027 at 10:35, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:")

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tailored rate carveout for LunarMed pilot — VP/CFO signoff requested

Appreciate the quick finance review, Marissa — that framing works. I pushed back with the customer and proposed the your alternate structure (40% initial discount + $150k onboarding credit tied to milestones). They countered asking if we can add a modest SLA credit if we don’t hit onboarding timelines, instead of deeper discounting — they prefer outcome-based protections.

Suggested compromise (for leadership):
- Offer: 40% discount months 0–6; onboarding credit $150k payable on milestone acceptance; SLA delivery credit (capped at 10% monthly invoice for missed milestones) as a swap for deeper % discounts.
- Contractual guardrails: 70% usage threshold at month 6 for discount retention; onboarding credit clawback pro rata if thresholds not met; 12-month minimum commitment to enable onboarding credit.

Next steps: If finance and legal are good with the wording I’ll circulate an updated SOW + track changes to legal and get LunarMed to sign. If leadership signs off we can send a redlined commercial term sheet to Priya and Sam after my Monday call.

Thanks,
Soojin
(attachment: proposed_sow_20270425.docx)

(quoted: "On Fri, 23 Apr 2027 at 14:02, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:")

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tailored rate carveout for LunarMed pilot — VP/CFO signoff requested

Team — reviewed the thread and Finance memo. Given the strategic nature of the logo and the ARR profile, I am willing to provide conditional signoff on the proposed compromise:  

- Approve offering: 40% discount months 0–6 + $150k onboarding credit tied to milestone acceptance; SLA credit language ok as proposed (cap 10% monthly invoice).
- Conditions: incorporate a clawback clause that recoups onboarding credit pro rata if usage < 70% of committed units over the first 6 months; include a rollback to published rates if customer delays deployment > 90 days without cause.
- Require: Legal to add explicit audit rights for first 12 months and a right to validate usage reporting; Sales to include an internal one-page exec summary to be stored on the deal record.

Once Legal signs the updated SOW, Finance will release the onboarding credit. Ben / Soojin — this is time-sensitive; if they accept, get the updated commercial term sheet to me for a final sign-off stamp.

Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Commercial Finance
